messages.content:
Diagnosis:
The failing test calls ClassUtils.getShortClassName(Class) with an array class (String[].class) and expects "String[]". The current bug report states that when this method is invoked on array types, a semicolon is improperly appended to the class name (e.g., "String;").

Looking at the implementation of getShortClassName(Class<?> cls), it simply calls getShortClassName(cls.getName()) which is the version that takes a String representing the class name.

The getShortClassName(String className) method is supposed to parse the class name string and extract the short class name. However, this method does not appear to handle array notation correctly. It tries to find the last dot '.' to find package separators and then extracts the substring after it, as well as handling inner class separators.

The problem is that for array classes, the name string is in the form of "[Ljava.lang.String;", which is the internal JVM notation for an array of type String. The current method doesn't do any special parsing to handle the leading '[L' and trailing ';' that annotate arrays in the class name string format.

Therefore, it returns the substring after the last dot including the trailing semicolon, causing "String;" to be returned instead of "String[]". The source of the semicolon in the returned string is the original class name string that encodes array notation.

The current bug report confirms this observation and states that a semicolon is introduced at the end of the short class name for arrays.

Hence, the root cause is that getShortClassName(String) does not properly decode the JVM internal name of an array class, leaving the internal array encoding (especially the trailing semicolon) in the returned short class name. There is an indicated TODO/comment in the code about "Handle array encoding // Strip Object type encoding" which currently is not implemented.

No relevant information from recent bug reports was found, as they are unrelated issues.

In summary, the bug happens because the internal class name for arrays is not being decoded properly by getShortClassName(String).

The failing test expects "String[]" (the human-readable form for the array) but gets "String;" with a trailing semicolon due to JVM internal array notation in the class name string.

This explains the test failure and bug report exactly. The code is missing logic to convert internal array naming to a readable notation with brackets instead of semicolons.

The fix should be located in ClassUtils.getShortClassName(String), adding special handling for array types to translate the internal "[Lclassname;" form to "classname[]".

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
